capabilities: Import images by drag, paste, file or URL
Organize images with tags, annotations and star ratings
Browse galleries in mosaic, grid and list modes
Connect images to notes and create native Canvas files
Export, transfer and deduplicate catalog images
extras: Desktop only, with Windows as the tested platform; the interface starts in Portuguese; distributed through GitHub releases rather than the Obsidian Community Plugins listing; catalogs are JSON files with an adjacent assets folder that must be backed up together; no AI, paid service, account or background sync is used.
intentEvidence: Grimarium is its successor, with independent local editing.
motivation: Built as a successor to the discontinued Grimorio Catalog integration, offering independent local editing instead of relying on the external Grimorio application.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to browse, tag and annotate a collection of images without creating a Markdown note for each one.

relations.evidence: Grimarium is its successor, with independent local editing.
Grimorio Catalog was the earlier integration with the external Grimorio application. Grimarium is its successor

summary: Local image library that keeps images as real vault files and organizes them with tags, annotations, ratings, note links and Canvas export.
